cells.tense: The direction is set and the walking has started, right here where you stand.
cells.ask: Before you say the next big decision out loud, write what you know about it and give the page a day. Then decide where people can hear you.
cells.core: A heading gets picked and the walking starts — no argument, no buildup, just motion with a place it's going. In good order that means a direction held without gripping, kept through resistance without getting eaten by it. The aim stays the aim and the pace stays steady.\n\nThe quiet before you speak is part of it. Something lands before you announce it, and you give it that room. That gap does real work; it's why what you decide holds up once it's out. Keep the margin. Say the thing after it has landed, not while it is still landing, and the way you move stays yours to use.
cells.sheetLine: You decide whole and move on it. Keep the quiet before you say it.
cells.verb: to move with a clarity that doesn't need to argue
cells.place: out on the road with the destination set

cells.tense: You're already living past the decision, braced for the version where it comes out right.
cells.ask: Take the one thing you're most braced about. Write what would count as it going fine, then close the notebook and don't check it for a week.
cells.core: In working order this is clean motion toward a destination — a heading held, a pace kept, resistance that neither scatters it nor eats it. You can walk it with people around without needing their agreement first. The aim stays the aim.\n\nYou're living past that now, rehearsing a day that hasn't arrived. So you plan, argue, lay track ahead of ground that isn't there, and check the plan again. The momentum is real; it's just spending itself on tomorrow. Write what would count as the thing going fine, put the notebook away, and leave it a week. Direction survives being left alone.
cells.sheetLine: You're planning a future you can't write in. Write it down and stop checking.

cells.tense: You're standing at a door that's already behind you, and the road ahead looks quiet.
cells.ask: Take the one thing you keep circling and build the smallest real piece of it today — the draft, the call, the first hour you can hold.
cells.core: Working direction is momentum with a destination — not aggression, just focused motion that keeps its heading through resistance. From out here that looks plain: you pick a place to go, you walk, you arrive. You don't need to feel charged to do it; the motion carries the feeling.\n\nRight now the direction is set but nothing is moving on it, and standing still has started to feel like the road went quiet. It didn't. Build the smallest real piece of the thing — the draft, the call, the first hour — today, where it can be seen. Direction comes back through your hands, not through deciding again. One piece is enough to pull the current through.
cells.sheetLine: You already decided. Build the smallest real piece of it today.

cells.tense: Things move when you're in the room, and you keep calling that just how the week went.
cells.ask: Name one thing that only moved because you moved it. Say the sentence to yourself once, without adding anything after it.
cells.core: The working face is structure that serves what it organizes — clear, reliable, felt in your presence. Things make sense when you're there. A direction holds, decisions get made, and people can feel the shape of what's next. That is the thing doing what it's for.\n\nYou don't count it that way. You'd tell it as the situation, the timing, what other people were already going to do. The momentum in the room is yours; you carry it and don't call it carrying. Say one of them out loud to yourself: that thing moved because you moved it. Nothing after the sentence. Let one true thing stand without stepping around it.
cells.sheetLine: Things move because you move them. You just don't say so.
